Nightwarden Minthara[1] Baenre is a recruitable[2] Companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. She is a Lolth-Sworn Drow[3] and an Oath of Vengeance Paladin with the Noble background.

Ruthless in service of the Absolute, she commands a camp of goblins planning an attack on the Emerald Grove in the name of their god. Initially hostile, she can be re-encountered during Act Two and saved from execution.

“
Bhaal, Lolth... the Absolute. They do not have followers - they only have victims, and they reward devotion with death.
„
— Minthara, on gods

Overview

For a full overview of Minthara's starting features, see the articles Paladin, Oath of Vengeance, and Lolth-sworn drow.

Background

A member of the ancient  House Baenre, Minthara is a True Soul in service of the Absolute. She is one of the three leaders of the Goblin Camp in the Wilderness. She and her fellow True Souls,  Priestess Gut and  Dror Ragzlin, set up a base of operations in an old Selûnite temple in search of a  Mysterious Artefact by order of  Ketheric Thorm.[4]

Starting class

Before she is recruited, Minthara is a level 6 paladin with the following Ability Scores: 16 STR, 15 DEX, 14 CON, 10 INT, 12 WIS, 17 CHA. If recruited, Minthara reverts to a level 1 Oath of Vengeance paladin with the standard ability scores for that Class, and a focus on dual-wielding one-handed weapons. This presents an offence-oriented toolkit with many ways to control and debuff foes.

Special features

Minthara's passive  Soul Branding allows her to grant herself or an ally an additional 5 m / 17 ft of movement and 2d4 + 1⁠⁠Fire damage on their next attack. She also bears the Brand of the Absolute and can fully benefit from items with this effect. Furthermore, she has access to the following illithid powers:

  •  Charm
  •  Concentrated Blast
  •  Favourable Beginnings
  •  Psionic Backlash

Personal quest

Minthara does not have a personal quest like other companions. However, she is directly involved in other important quests.

As part of the main-quest ⁠Save the Refugees, the party can decide which side to support in the conflict between the goblins and druids of the grove. If siding with the druids and refugees, Minthara becomes hostile and is an objective of ⁠Defeat the Goblins. If siding with the Absolute, she appears as an ally during ⁠Raid the Grove. If the grove remains sealed the day of the raid, she instructs her raiders to kill the party.

In ⁠Decide Minthara's Fate, the party can decide what happens to Minthara after her trial at the hands of  Ketheric Thorm and  Disciple Z'rell at Moonrise Towers.[5].

After recruiting Minthara, she has a personal interest in destroying the Cult of the Absolute and killing  Orin the Red for revenge, therefore completing ⁠Get Orin's Netherstone. Orin killed Minthara's drow companions and tortured and enslaved her to the Cult of the Absolute through implanting a tadpole in Minthara's brain. The Cult of the Absolute forced Minthara to commit massacres on their enemies.

Recruitment

Act One

Although Minthara can be first encountered in Act One, she cannot be recruited as a permanent companion before reaching Moonrise Towers in Act Two.[6][7]

If the party side with Minthara during ⁠Save the Refugees and raid the grove with her, no additional steps are needed to ensure she appears at Moonrise Towers.

If the party side with the druids, Minthara must be  Knocked Out when fought. This can be done in the Shattered Sanctum or when defending the grove from the goblin attack.[8]

Act Two

If Minthara survives the events of Act One, she can be found at Moonrise Towers facing trial by Ketheric Thorm for failing to find the Mysterious Artefact. Sentenced to death, Minthara is taken to Moonrise Towers Prison to be tortured until her execution. The party can help her escape and, if invited to camp, she can be recruited to the party.

“
The drow is unpredictable, uncompromising. I respect her almost as much as I distrust her.
„
— Lae'zel, speaking to the player character after Minthara is recruited

Approval

Main article: Minthara/Approval

Minthara approves of displays of power and control, often in the form of violent, if not efficient, solutions to problems. She respects those with the strength to follow their own will, and enjoys cruel irony on occasion.[verify]

Minthara dislikes shows of compassion, especially towards those she considers weak. She disapproves of any form of benevolence without something to gain for it, as well as senseless violence that does not aid the party in some way. Above all, she despises acts of weakness and any worship of Lolth.

Romance

Main article: Minthara/Romance

If the player character sides with the Absolutists and successfully raids the Emerald Grove, they can have a one-night stand with Minthara while celebrating their victory.

Should Minthara be saved and recruited, she can be romanced by characters of any gender. Though initially cold, Minthara may eventually reveal some of her deepest fears to her partner, and may also display a more romantic, if not jealous, side of her.

Description

Appearance

With a stern countenance, piercing eyes, and a low, regal and steady voice, Minthara has an imposing presence. Like most drow, she has purplish-blue skin, crimson eyes, pointed ears, and is lithe of frame with delicate features. Familiar with combat, she remains trim and fit, and carries herself with a measure of confidence not uncommon to many nobles. Her hair is silver with light gold highlights kept in a loosely arranged top bun, with stray strands adorning the sides of her face. On the left side of her neck, she bears the seal of  House Baenre in black, marking her a member of the ancestral house. Her equipment is of the finest quality, and her at-ease clothes reflect some of her noble upbringing. Given all of these things, Minthara is found quite attractive by many and, like Shadowheart, she is fully aware of these perceptions.[9]

Personality

As a Lolth-sworn drow and follower of the Absolute, Minthara typically has a highly hostile and cruel attitude towards other beings,[10] considering almost everyone as inferior. She has a special disdain for those who do not share her beliefs, and holds other drow in high regard. Her upbringing as a noble in  Menzoberranzan further compounds her superiority complex. Aligned with the Absolute, she is willing to do whatever it takes to serve it.

Prideful,[11] Power hungry[12] and a product of her drow upbringing, she is always looking for ways to increase her standing among her peers. Previously a follower of Lolth, she also knows that violence, deception, and cruelty are effective tools to obtain what she wants, and are tools she has considerable experience with.

Despite her overt dislike for others, as a result of her constant striving for power and influence, Minthara knows to "read the room". She:

  • Is observant, always studying those around and surrounding her
  • Often understands the plights of her companions, even if she may not care for them
  • Is always willing to offer a solution in her own way; though her methods are sometimes extreme, they always have sound reasoning
  • Does not support mindless cruelty if it serves no purpose, and even shows a weak spot for  Scratch

If romanced, Minthara may reveal that she harbours doubts about her life and circumstances.

Whether due to her looks, power and influence or attitude, Minthara concedes she has had several past lovers[13] and, unbeknownst to her, even has a few suitors amongst the goblins.[14][15]

If recruited and freed from the Absolute's influence, Minthara's cruelty becomes more tempered, and her fury is aimed solely at other leaders of the Cult - particularly  Orin the Red. She becomes contemplative of her actions under the Absolute's influence, and rues their exploitation of her fears and yearning for belonging to use her as a tool.

History

Menzoberranzan

Born into the ancient  House Baenre of Menzoberranzan, Minthara was raised as a noble of the city in  Qu'ellarz'orl, a plateau above the city expanse.[16] Taught in the ways of  Lolth, she rose to be an important house matron, enjoying all the luxuries of her birthright.[17] She survived her first assassination attempt as a child, and another at the hands of her mother when she came of age.[18]

Sometime during her life there, Minthara encountered a True Soul and two novices preaching the message of the Absolute. Minthara hanged and displayed them as a warning against heresy,[19] but curiosity got the best of her and, after using necromancy on the corpses to find their base of operations, she prepared a retinue of warriors to strike at Moonrise Towers.

Indoctrination and time in the Cult

Minthara gathered her allies to battle the absolutists. Yet, when they arrived at the Moonrise Towers, they were met with a lavish feast and a welcome fit for a house matron.  Ketheric Thorm had been expecting her, and invited her to partake of his feast alongside  Orin the Red. He explained that he wished to form an alliance between Moonrise and Menzoberranzan, flattering Minthara and playing to her pride.[20] Lowering her guard, Minthara was unable to react in time as Orin jumped on the table and sliced her men's throats as she approached her. Standing before her, Orin expressed her interest in Minthara, and Ketheric approved, ordering her to be taken to the Mind Flayer Colony.[21] There, Minthara was held for some time, helplessly watching as her men were processed for food or turned into thralls. Eventually, Orin returned and placed a tadpole in Minthara's eye, sealing the drow's fate as part of the Cult of the Absolute.[22]

Under orders of her new god, Minthara participated in many massacres carried out by the cult, mostly against religious communities who refused to be converted. She became a zealot, and in time, even began to admire Orin. Orin would manipulate her further, telling her lies of how she was a True Soul, chosen by the Absolute as her greatest weapon.[23] For Minthara, the Absolute was more than just a god, it was everything she ever truly wanted.[23] With a new purpose, Minthara proceeded to the Wilderness in search of a powerful weapon her new goddess desires, hungry to prove herself.

Involvement

Act One

Minthara is first encountered at the Shattered Sanctum within the Goblin Camp, planning an attack on Emerald Grove at the behest of the Absolute. When spoken to, she quickly identifies the player character as a fellow True Soul, and reveals she believes the druids are hiding a powerful weapon that the Absolute desires. She has been surveying the land in search of the weapon, sending scouts to track the leader of the grove, Halsin.[24] Minthara probes the party's minds with her tadpole, possibly exposing the grove's location.

Save the Refugees

Though Minthara does not have a personal quest, she is deeply involved in ⁠Save the Refugees. The party can kill Minthara as part of the quest ⁠Defeat the Goblins. With one of the three goblin leaders dead,  Dror Ragzlin and  Priestess Gut would be next.

Raiding the Grove

Alternatively, the party can agree to disclose the grove's location and raid it with the Absolutists, which initiates ⁠Raid the Emerald Grove.[verify] Minthara then moves to the inner gates of the Shattered Sanctum and disappears from there after being spoken with. She also disappears if the party venture to another area (i.e. the Worg Pens or the Goblin Camp or using fast travel). Even if she is knocked out before disappearing, the raid still triggers. Dror Ragzlin and Gut can still be killed after Minthara has left without her becoming hostile. The raid on the grove begins after the next Long Rest. Completing the raid causes  Karlach and  Wyll to permanently leave the party.

After the grove is destroyed, Minthara and the goblins join the party at their camp to celebrate slaughtering the druids, even though they failed to find the weapon the Absolute desired. Minthara also offers a casual night of pleasure with the player character. Rejecting her offer angers her, but carries no negative consequences.

After the celebrations, Minthara urges the party to join the Absolute at Moonrise Towers in the Shadow-Cursed Lands. She gives the party her  Spider's Lyre to summon a guide that helps them through the deadly shadows, and she departs shortly after.

Double-Crossing Minthara

After initiating the raid on the grove, it is possible to double-cross her. To do so, during the raid of the Emerald Grove, the party must side with the tieflings. If the goblin forces are defeated and Minthara is killed or knocked out, then the quests ⁠Rescue the Druid Halsin and ⁠Defeat the Goblins are completed without having to kill or  knock out Dror Ragzlin and Gut.

Act Two

Decide Minthara's Fate

Should Minthara survive Act One, whether friendly or hostile, she can be encountered in Moonrise Towers on trial by Ketheric Thorm for failing to retrieve the  Mysterious Artefact. The party can intervene on her behalf, but Ketheric sentences her to death regardless of what is said. This begins the quest ⁠Decide Minthara's Fate.

As Minthara is dragged away by the guards, the party can follow and find her at the Moonrise Towers Prison, undergoing torture by two gnome inquisitors. If both gnomes are killed beforehand, they will be replaced with the human and half-orc Absolutist clerics  Nola and  Mola. The party can join the questioners in erasing Minthara's mind, turning her into a witless thrall of the Absolute, or help her escape, either by slaying the gnomes or through dialogue. If Minthara is freed, the party must escort her out of the prison, through any combination of stealth, dialogue or violence.[25] Once freed, Minthara can leave or be permitted to join the party, at which point she joins the camp. However, she temporarily leaves the party whenever they venture back to regions in Act One.

If told to go her own way, Minthara disappears, and does not return until after defeating Ketheric Thorm at the end of Act Two. After taking the portal from the mind flayer colony, she can be found sitting on his throne inside Moonrise Towers. At this point there is another opportunity to accept her as a companion or tell her again to go her own way, rebuffing her offer once more.[verify]

If the party locate  Isobel for the Absolutists and allow  Balthazar to take the  Nightsong during ⁠Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic, an audience is granted with Ketheric Thorm, who allows the party to pray at the altar of the Absolute. Doing so ultimately results in the party's imprisonment in pods in the Mind Flayer Colony, where Balthazar attempts to turn them into zombies at his service. In the ensuing fight, the party may battle a Zombie Dror Ragzlin and Zombie Minthara, if either died during prior events.

Freeing and recruiting Minthara gains the following inspirations:

  • ⁠Nobleborn as Below, so Above ( Noble background)
  • ⁠Twice Scorned, Twice Abandoned ( Urchin background)

Act Three

Minthara is one of the possible victims of Orin's kidnapping during Act Three as part of ⁠Rescue Orin's Victim. If so, once Orin is defeated and Minthara rescued, she comments on the entire ordeal. Additionally, she expresses feeling disheartened after killing her former abuser. Although Orin could only copy the surface characteristics of her victims, Minthara saw herself in Orin's bloodlust and madness, a shattered but possible version of herself had she not broken free from the Absolute's control.

Get Orin's Netherstone

Having been indoctrinated into the Cult of the Absolute by Orin herself, Minthara has a personal stake in the quest ⁠Get Orin's Netherstone.

Endings

When spoken to in either ending, Minthara bemoans the party's lack of extravagance and asks if the player character regrets their decision not to control the Absolute. Ambient chatter from Minthara has her wryly suspecting there have been other reunions to which she has not been invited, that all the heroes gathering together paints a target on the party for hostile attack, and that she is becoming accustomed to the taste of surface-grown plants.

Return to Menzoberranzan

Minthara can be encouraged to return to Menzoberranzan, to which she will agree, suggesting they put the gnomes back to work to rebuild the Steel Watch, returning as conquerors to found a new noble House. Six months after the fall of the absolutists, Minthara mentions the war against House Baenre is going well, but she welcomes the distraction of  Withers' party.

Baldur's Gate

Otherwise, if encouraged to stay in Baldur's Gate, Minthara proclaims Baldur's Gate needs new leadership which she is happy to provide. She shares that she has been scheming in the shadows and the political intrigue has been enjoyable. She asserts that the people will learn from her or bow to her.

Quest rewards

  • Assassin's Touch - given by Minthara for escorting the goblin  Sazza to the Goblin Camp and convincing her to spare her life.
  • Gift from the Absolute — given by Minthara for siding with the absolutists and raiding the grove.
  • Spider's Lyre — given by Minthara after the camp celebration upon successfully raiding the grove, or looted from her if killed or knocked out during Act One.

Interactions

Companion interactions

Minthara has unique dialogue interactions as a companion available after certain events. Whenever one is available, a floating [!] icon is visible above her.

Act Two

  • Upon arrival at the camp as a companion, she has dialogue about her time under the Absolute and her vow of vengeance. If she joins the party while she still has unfinished dialogue, she asks the player character for privacy and cuts them out of this dialogue.
  • After defeating Ketheric, Minthara sits on his throne, gloating. When spoken to, she reveals more about her indoctrination into the Cult, and her plans after the Cult is destroyed.

Act Three

  • Upon reaching Rivington, Minthara comments on the state of the refugees and city's refusal to let them in.
  • If pursuing a romance with her, she asks about the player character's thoughts on her.

Unique interactions

As a companion, Minthara has unique interactions and special dialogue with  Viconia DeVir in Act Three. She also has has special dialogue if Viconia is mentioned with her in Act Two.

Combat

Main article: Minthara/Combat

Loot

Minthara possesses the same items as her starting equipment, except for her underwear. If knocked unconscious, she does not drop a  Mind Flayer Parasite nor a supply pack.[26]

If all equipment and clothing are looted from her and she is left unconscious, she reappears in Act Two at Moonrise Towers in a new set of camp clothes including camp shoes and underwear.

Idle banter

At the goblin camp, Minthara can be found talking to  Rozzak:

  • Rozzak
    Wot are we waitin' for? Spears are sharp, the lads are all riled up an' ready!
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    You have already failed me once, and now you dare question me?
  • Rozzak
    I, er... didn't mean nothin' by it, yer ladyship. Honest I didn't.
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    Your life, much like your words, is meaningless, whelp. End the latter to save the former.
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    The village to the east - it's abandoned?
  • Rozzak
    Looks that way. But scouts said they heard somethin' movin' around out there. Somethin' big.
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    It's not our concern. Our prey are elsewhere.
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    How many raiders do we have?
  • Rozzak
    Plenty of lashers, loads of hunters... and a few pariahs to carry the powder kegs.
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    These pariahs - they're prepared to fight for the Absolute?
  • Rozzak
    What they do ain't exactly fightin'. All they gotta do is light up their powder and burn.
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    Then they're prepared to die for the Absolute. Good.
  • Rozzak
    Dyin's the only thing they're good at.
  • Rozzak
    Prisoner'll talk, yer ladyship. Spike always makes 'em talk. (After Zurga reports to Minthara)
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    If he doesn't, I'll cut out his tongue.
  • Rozzak
    If he don't have a tongue, he can't tell us nothin'!
  • Nightwarden Minthara
    The prisoner can keep his tongue - it's Spike's I'll be removing.

Speak with Dead

  • Who were you before the Absolute claimed you?
    • Nightwarden Minthara
      Destined to be... matron mother... House Baenre...
  • Why did you abandon Lolth?
    • Nightwarden Minthara
      For the Absolute's lie...
  • What were your ambitions before you died?
    • Nightwarden Minthara
      To find a home...
  • Where are you from?
    • Nightwarden Minthara
      Menzoberranzan...
  • How do you want to be remembered?
    • Nightwarden Minthara
      The commander I was... not the slave... I became...
  • Have you left anything unsaid or undone?
    • Nightwarden Minthara
      Murdering Orin...

Notes and references

[27]
  1. ↑ In traditional Drow names, the prefix "Min-" means "lesser", "minor", or "second", while the suffix "-thara" means "glyph", "marker", or "rune". Owen K.C. Stephens, "By Any Other Name: The Drow", Dragon 267 (January 2000): 28-31
  2. ↑ Minthara went through some recruitment changes during development and after release. Intended to be recruited only if the grove was destroyed, prior to Patch 5, an exploit could be used to recruit Minthara when siding with the grove. Minthara had to be knocked out temporarily in Act 1, recovering after a long rest. Once the party reached Act 2 and acquired the spells  Polymorph and  Dominate Beast, they had to return to Shattered Sanctum, turn her into a sheep and dominate her. The party then had to fast-travel back to the Moonrise Towers and then had to move Minthara as a sheep into the throne room, where the judgement continued as if Minthara was alive. After the cutscene she would be transported to the dungeon. The party had to attack her quickly once imprisoned as she would begin to run away otherwise, and then turn invisible and exit combat. Minthara was then part of the interrogation scene and her recruitment could proceed as normal.
    When Patch 5 was introduced, Minthara could be recruited if she was knocked out temporarily at her camp in the Shattered Sanctum, dealing with the rest of the goblin camp without long rests in-between as the game files checked for both conditions in order to trigger her scene at Moonrise Towers.
    Patch 6 removed the requirement for Minthara being temporarily hostile / knocked out. The game no longer checks for that condition. It became possible to recruit Minthara through knocking her out when defending the grove from the goblin attack. However, if Minthara was knocked out in the goblin camp, the quest ⁠Defeat the Goblins had to be finished prior to taking a Long Rest.
    Since Patch 7, all methods of knocking her out result in a recruitment opportunity.
  3. ↑ If the player character is a Lolth-sworn drow, many unique dialogue options are available, one of which includes condemning Minthara and attacking her for abandoning Lolth.
  4. ↑  Attracting Drow Exiles in Kethric Thorm's quarters.
  5. ↑ If Minthara is recruited as a companion and returns to Moonrise Towers while Ketheric Thorm is still alive, and she is not near the player character or another tadpole-infected companion, she will be (whether disguised or not) attacked if seen by tower guards or other principal followers of the Absolute. If other party members are nearby, they may be drawn into the conflict as well. The exact range required to avoid a fight is not yet known, but if avoiding one is desired, it is recommended that companion Minthara remain within sight of a tadpoled party member while in Moonrise Towers.
  6. ↑ If recruited, returning to Act One areas with Minthara in the active party causes her to leave the party. This can be circumvented by casting  Silence on her before doing so. Minthara's limitation on travel between Acts and areas may have arisen because it is possible that, during development, she was intended to be a companion earlier than she ended up being for release. Therefore, travelling to Act One (once recruited in Act Two), while likely an originally intended behaviour for Minthara, was later revised and can now only be accomplished by exploit. This assertion is supported by the following:
    • Point one: Minthara refuses to travel to Act One with the party unless silenced immediately prior. Normally, just prior to travel there, Minthara says, "If you intend to stray from Moonrise while Ketheric still lives, I shall remain at camp, strategising his downfall." The player character may respond with, "I have unfinished business to attend to before dealing with Ketrheric", upon which she replies, "I do not. All that I did before you rescued me was as a puppet of the Absolute - it is behind me. Until Ketheric falls, only vengeance remains."
    • Point two: if the party returns to Act One without Minthara, all unequipped items in her inventory are removed and placed in a backpack in the inventory of the player character.
    • Point three: Minthara has exploration lines for Rosymorn Monastery and the destruction sequence of the weapon on the rooftop. She also has an exploration line at the Nautiloid. Additionally, coded into the game's dialogue files are various points in Crèche Y'llek where the player character can gain or lose approval with Minthara, even though she can only be recruited later in Act Two and cannot travel back to Crèche Y'llek without use of an exploit.
    • Point four: if the party returns to Act One with Minthara, she has no tent at camp.
  7. ↑ There is currently a bug involving Minthara if the party return to Act One.[verify] It works as follows: If Minthara is recruited while the player character is  disguised and the party venture to an Act One area without Minthara in the active party roster, upon returning to Act Two, at camp Minthara behaves as if being a merchant who has -45 attitude with the player character. She does not speak with the player character (and therefore cannot rejoin the active party roster) until given enough gold or items of value through the barter window until her attitude is -19 or better (i.e., in the "yellow" area of the approval scale). Once this threshold is passed she can be brought back into the active party and interacted with as normal - and with her normal approval. To avoid this bug, either Minthara must be silenced before proceeding to Act One and have her in the active party or, upon returning, have the player character speak with her in the same disguise form they were using when she was recruited.
  8. ↑ As long as she is knocked out in the Shattered Sanctum, it is possible to complete ⁠Defeat the Goblins after several long rests without compromising her recruitment in Act Two.
  9. ↑ In Act Three, if playing the Dark Urge, the player character can reveal they are a Bhaalspawn to Minthara and, via their tadpole, share visions of their grotesque thoughts and deeds with her. After doing so, she remarks in awe, "Elgg-hor... duk-tak... slayer. There are many names for you, and all of them inspire dread. You are exquisite." If responding with, "So are you", Minthara answers with a grin, "I know."
  10. ↑ If Minthara is recruited and asked about her thoughts on Shadowheart, then asked what she has against  Shar, she reveals, "I have performed a thousand interrogations, squeezing out the most-guarded secrets held in heart, mind and soul. I can tell you this – when the trivial parts have been whittled away and I have sifted out what remains, in most cases a person amounts to nothing at all."
  11. ↑ If, after the party vanquish Ketheric Thorm for good, a recruited Minthara is asked about how she first encountered the Absolute, she relates how a true soul acolyte and their novices visited her in Menzoberranzen, preaching togetherness. After hanging them, she went to investigate Moonrise Towers with the intent of waging war on the Absolute. If the player character responds with "Given how we met, it's safe to say you failed", Minthara irritably replies, "It is never safe to point out my shortcomings, iblith." Later in the same conversation when Minthara explains how she was captured there, the player charater can point out "Pride can be a great weakness", to which Minthara agrees, "I recognise my flaws - pride is certainly among them."
  12. ↑ If Minthara is rescued from Moonrise Towers and joins the party, the player character can speak with her about her paladin vows. If they do and challenge her vows as being hypocritical, Minthara ultimately responds, "I do not know what will happen to with my vows when I defeat all those who serve the Absolute. I do know that when I take the Absolute's power, I will not lose control of it as our enemies have. I will harness it to create a more perfect world.
